newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, eyes LME Third Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, eyes LME Third Wednesday.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly weaker in light volume after a mid-session attempt to move higher quickly fizzled.
Dealers noted that in spite of leading players covering some of their short positions, red metal futures on both sides of the Atlantic settled barely changed.
September COMEX copper went out 0.05 cent lower at 104.30 cents a lb, traded 104.90 to 103.00 cents. Spot July settled 1.15 cents firmer at 108.05 cents.

The dramatic collapse in copper prices over the past week, which probably stemmed from more than just a technical correction, has made it difficult to see where prices were headed short-term, Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
"The fierceness of the collapse was so strong that it may not be over," Hirsch said.
The sharp fall in prices comes at a time of rising LME stocks and a summer seasonal slowdown in the U.S. and Europe.
September COMEX ended the week almost seven cents weaker after a sharp selloff on Tuesday and Wednesdsay.
The LME cash to three months backwardation ended at $137/$140 a tonne after holding on to the day's gains of $10 to $20.
The market was still nervous over the outcome of "Third Wednesday" pricing on LME, which takes place on Monday.
The market's backwardation was overlapping the key Third Wednesay pricing date with its unknown number of unresolved positions adding to nervousness, dealers said.
The Third Wednesday refers to the only date in each month that could be traded beyond 90-days.
Meanwhile LME stocks continued to rise, up 2,800 tonnes Friday to 139,125 tonnes, partly a reflection of metal moving from COMEX to the London exchange due to arbitrage, dealers said.
COMEX stocks haeve fallen sharply in past weeks, and were down 995 short tons to 35,454 short tons Friday.
